title: The Vrishnis Resolve to Abandon Mathura for Dwarka
one_line_summary: Fearing Kalayavana's assault, the Vrishnis and Andhakas make Krishna their president and resolve to leave Mathura for Kushasthali (Dwarka).
source_excerpt: Thereupon starting for Mathura with one Akshouhini of soldiers Kalayavana sent his messenger to the house of Vrishnis and Andhakas... being united the Vrishnis and Andhakas, making the highly intelligent Krishna their president, held a conference in fear of Kalayavana... resolved upon flying away from the charming city of Mathura and thought of settling down in Kushasthali Dwarka.
notes: Told in a forward-looking summary within the genealogical chapter on Vasudeva's family (chapter XXXV). | [citation-repair: content matches the Kalayavana-era flight (~ch 113); printed locator 35 does not contain this passage]

title: The Sun God Grants Satrajit the Syamantaka Jewel
one_line_summary: Worshipping the sun on the ocean bank, Satrajit is granted the peerless Syamantaka jewel by the sun god.
source_excerpt: Thereupon the lord took out from his neck the peerless jewel Swyamantaka and gave it to him. Thereupon Bhaskara gave him the jewel Swyamantaka.
variant_notes: The text alternates between Prasena and Satrajit as the jewel's recipient; Satrajit then confers the jewel on his brother Prasena.

title: Prasena Is Slain for the Jewel; Jambavan Takes It
one_line_summary: Prasena, wearing the Syamantaka, is killed by a lion; a bear (Jambavan) slays the lion and carries the jewel into his den.
source_excerpt: Once on a time adorned with that jewel Prasena went out a-hunting. He was, for that Swyamantaka, slain by a wild lion. Killing that flying lion a highly powerful bear took that jewel and entered into his den.

title: The Vrishnis Suspect Krishna of Stealing the Jewel
one_line_summary: Hearing of Prasena's death, the Vrishnis and Andhakas suspect Krishna of stealing the Syamantaka; the innocent Krishna resolves to recover it.
source_excerpt: Hearing of the death of Prasena, all the members of Vrishni and Andhaka families entertained suspicions against Krishna, because they knew that he had a fancy for that jewel.

title: Krishna Wrestles Jambavan for Twenty-One Days
one_line_summary: Krishna enters the bear's den and wrestles Jambavan for twenty-one days, defeating him, marrying Jambavati, and taking the jewel.
source_excerpt: Govinda wrestled with Jamvavan in that den for twenty-one days... Having vanquished the highly powerful Jamvavan he married the most beloved daughter of the king of bears by name Jamvavati and took away the jewel for clearing himself.

title: Krishna Returns the Jewel and Clears His Name
one_line_summary: Krishna brings back the Syamantaka and hands it to Satrajit in the assembly of the Satwatas, clearing himself of the false charge.
source_excerpt: Having thus brought the jewel and cleared himself of the charge he handed over Swyamantaka to Satrajit in an assembly of the Satwatas.

title: Shatadhanwa Murders Satrajit and Gives the Jewel to Akrura
one_line_summary: Shatadhanwa slays Satrajit at night, steals the Syamantaka, and secretly gives it to Akrura.
source_excerpt: Thereupon, having slain Satrajit at the dead of night the highly powerful Shatadhanwa took away the jewel and made a present of it to Akrura.

title: Krishna Pursues and Slays Shatadhanwa
one_line_summary: Krishna and Balarama pursue Shatadhanwa; Krishna kills him on foot near Mithila but does not find the jewel.
source_excerpt: going on foot, Achyuta (Krishna), highly skilled in the use of arms, killed Shatadhanwa on the way to Mithila... he did not see Swyamantaka.

title: Balarama Departs to Mithila in Anger
one_line_summary: Believing Krishna is withholding the jewel, Balarama angrily leaves for Mithila, where Duryodhana learns the use of clubs from him.
source_excerpt: Repeatedly exclaiming 'Fie on you, Fie on you,' he replied to Janarddana... 'I go away. I have nothing to do with you or other Vrishnis of Dwarka.'

title: Akrura's Exile Brings Drought; His Return Brings Rain
one_line_summary: After Akrura leaves Dwarka, Indra withholds rain and drought devastates the land; when he returns, the rains fall again.
source_excerpt: After the departure of Akrura Pakashasana did not pour rain... When the liberal Akrura returned to Dwarka the thousand-eyed Indra began to discharge showers on the bank of the ocean.

title: Krishna Reclaims the Jewel from Akrura and Returns It
one_line_summary: Krishna, discerning the jewel is with Akrura, asks for it in assembly; Akrura gives it up, and Krishna returns it to him.
source_excerpt: Thereupon at the words of Krishna the high-minded Akrura, without experiencing the least pain, gave him the jewel in the midst of the assembled Satwatas... Hari, the repressor of enemies, returned it to him with a delighted heart.

title: Narada Urges Vishnu to Descend to Earth
one_line_summary: Narada tells Vishnu that the gods' incarnations alone cannot destroy the demons reborn as kings, and urges him to descend himself.
source_excerpt: 'O Narayana, useless have been the incarnations of the gods for the destruction of the kings... Methinks their work cannot be accomplished without Narayana's Yoga.'

title: Vishnu Resolves to Be Born as a Cowherd
one_line_summary: Vishnu resolves to incarnate among men to destroy Kansa and the demons, and Brahma foretells his birth as Vasudeva's son among cowherds.
source_excerpt: Going to the region of men and assuming a human form I shall bring about the destruction of all those mighty demons headed by Kansa... Being born as a milkman with them he will live there happily.
notes: Printed as 'CHAPTER L.V. VISHNU'S REPLY' but contained within the chapter_054.txt file; cited by the printed chapter number (55). | [citation-repair: ch 55 absent from etext; re-cited to ch 54 by content match]

title: Narada Warns Kansa of His Doom
one_line_summary: Narada visits Kansa and reveals that Devaki's eighth child will be his death; Kansa scoffs and resolves to oppress the gods' followers.
source_excerpt: The child, of the eighth conception of your youngest sister Devaki who lives in Mathura, will be your death.

title: Kansa Orders the Destruction of Devaki's Children
one_line_summary: Fearing the prophecy, Kansa commands his ministers to guard Devaki and destroy her embryos from the very beginning.
source_excerpt: 'Do ye always be on your guard for destroying the (eight born) children of Devaki... destroy all the embryos of Devaki.'

title: The Saragarbha Demons Are Doomed to Be Born and Slain
one_line_summary: The six Saragarbha demons, cursed by Hiranyakashipu, are destined to be born from Devaki and killed by Kansa; Vishnu places their vital breaths in Devaki's womb.
source_excerpt: 'O ye great Asuras Saragarbhas, you all six will be born in order from Devaki and Kansa will kill you.'

title: Vishnu Commands Goddess Sleep to Arrange the Exchange
one_line_summary: Vishnu instructs the goddess Sleep (Yogamaya) to transfer the seventh embryo to Rohini and arrange the exchange of the eighth child with Yashoda's daughter.
source_excerpt: 'take that eldest brother of mine in the seventh month and place him within Rohini's womb... I will be taken to Yashoda and you will be taken to Devaki. By this our interchange Kansa will be stupified.'

title: Krishna Conjures Wolves to Move the Milkmen to Vrindavan
one_line_summary: Desiring a new forest, Krishna produces hundreds of wolves from his body to terrify the milkmen so they will abandon Vraja for Vrindavan.
source_excerpt: From the hairs of his body there arose hundreds of wolves living on fat, blood and flesh... striking terror to the entire land of milkmen.

title: Devaki's Seventh Embryo Is Transferred to Rohini
one_line_summary: The seventh embryo is transferred from Devaki to Rohini by the goddess of sleep, and the child is born as Sankarshana (Balarama).
source_excerpt: 'O fair one, I have extracted the embryo out of Devaki's womb and placed it in yours. Therefore this your son will be celebrated by the name of Sangkarshana.'

title: Krishna Is Born at Midnight Amid Cosmic Signs
one_line_summary: In the auspicious Abhijit muhurta at midnight, Devaki gives birth to Krishna, and the universe rejoices with divine signs.
source_excerpt: In the auspicious midnight and in Abhijit Muhurtta, Devaki gave birth to Vishnu and Yashoda to that daughter... the oceans were agitated, the pillars of the earth were shaken... Indra too, along with the gods, eulogised the glories of Madhusudhana.

title: Vasudeva Exchanges Krishna for Yashoda's Daughter
one_line_summary: At the divine command, Vasudeva carries the infant Krishna to Nanda's house and exchanges him for Yashoda's newborn daughter.
source_excerpt: Taking that boy, Vasudeva too, fond of his sons, speedily repaired to the house of Yashoda. Placing his son in her house against her knowledge he brought her daughter and placed her on Devaki's bedstead.

title: Kansa Dashes the Infant; Yogamaya Foretells His Death
one_line_summary: Kansa dashes the exchanged baby girl against a stone, but she rises into the sky as the goddess and warns that his destroyer is already born.
source_excerpt: Taking her with contempt by the legs and whirling her Kansa dashed her against a stone... 'O Kansa, for thy own destruction thou hast whirled and dashed me against a rock... I will tear off thy body with my hands and drink thy hot blood.'

title: Kansa Repents and Devaki Forgives Him
one_line_summary: Kansa, ashamed, confesses to Devaki and throws himself at her feet; Devaki forgives him, saying Time alone is the instrument.
source_excerpt: 'I throw myself at your feet like a son. Be not offended with me.'... Devaki said:—'I forgive you for the sin that you have committed by destroying my children.'

title: Krishna Overturns the Cart with His Foot
one_line_summary: The infant Krishna, left under a cart, overturns it with a kick of his foot while Yashoda is away.
source_excerpt: Then raising up his legs he overturned the carriage with one of them. And then crawling on his legs he began to cry for milk.

title: Krishna Sucks the Life Out of Putana
one_line_summary: The demoness Putana, disguised as a woman, tries to nurse Krishna with poisoned milk; he sucks out her life and she falls dead.
source_excerpt: Thereupon drinking up all her vital breaths together with her milk Krishna set up a terrible sound. She too, having her breast sundered, fell down earth.

title: Yashoda Binds Krishna; He Uproots the Arjuna Trees
one_line_summary: Yashoda ties Krishna to a mortar; he drags it between the twin Arjuna trees and uproots them, and is thereafter named Damodara.
source_excerpt: Placing that mortar between the two trees he began to drag it... those two Arjuna trees were uprooted with their roots and branches... From that day in which he was bound with the rope Krishna was called Damodara.

title: Balarama Slays the Demon Pralamva
one_line_summary: The demon Pralamva, disguised as a cowherd, carries Balarama away; prompted by Krishna, Balarama strikes him dead with his fist.
source_excerpt: with his well-formed fist resembling a thunder-bolt struck the wicked Pralamva on the head... on that Daitya... being slain, the celestials... gave him the name Baladeva after his action.

title: Krishna Resolves to Subdue the Serpent Kaliya
one_line_summary: Finding the Yamuna's lake poisoned by the serpent-king Kaliya, Krishna resolves to leap in and vanquish him.
source_excerpt: 'I should, however, vanquish this king of serpents... I shall climb this Kadamba tree, jump into the lake and vanquish Kalya.'

title: Krishna Leaps into the Yamuna to Face Kaliya
one_line_summary: Krishna climbs the Kadamba tree and plunges into Kaliya's lake, where the serpent and his attendants bind him in their coils.
source_excerpt: Climbing up to the top of the tree and emitting a leonine roar the cloud-hued and lotus-eyed Krishna jumped headlong down into the lake.

title: Krishna Dances on Kaliya's Hoods and Banishes Him
one_line_summary: Krishna breaks free, dances on the serpent's hoods, and banishes Kaliya to the ocean, restoring the Yamuna's waters.
source_excerpt: placing his feet on the hoods of the serpent-king that were above the water... he began to dance there... 'O serpent, I do not wish to allow you to live in this water of Yamuna. Therefore repair to the ocean with your wife and kinsmen.'

title: Krishna Persuades the Milkmen to Worship Govardhana
one_line_summary: Krishna argues that cowherds should worship the mountain and the kine rather than Indra, and wins over the milkmen.
source_excerpt: 'We are all milk-men who range in the forest. The precious kine constitute our subsistence. We should therefore worship the kine, the mountains and the forests.'
notes: | [citation-repair: ch 71 absent from etext; re-cited to ch 70 by content match]

title: Indra Sends the Storm Against Vrindavan
one_line_summary: Enraged by the suppression of his sacrifice, Indra sends the Samvartaka clouds to drown Vrindavan and its kine in seven nights of rain.
source_excerpt: 'Therefore within seven nights, distress, with rain and winds, the precious kine which constitute their life-long subsistence.'

title: Krishna Lifts Govardhana to Shelter the Gopas
one_line_summary: Krishna uproots mount Govardhana and holds it on his finger for seven nights as an umbrella sheltering the gopas and their kine.
source_excerpt: For protecting the Gopas like unto Brahma the Lord Krishna raised up that mountain and kept it on the tip of his finger.

title: Indra Descends and Installs Krishna as Govinda
one_line_summary: Indra comes down, eulogizes Krishna, and anoints him with heavenly water as the king of cows, naming him Govinda.
source_excerpt: Thereupon taking those jars full of heavenly water the king of gods... sprinkled Govinda... 'the people of this world will hymn thee as Govinda.'

title: Indra Asks Krishna to Befriend Arjuna
one_line_summary: Indra asks Krishna to protect his son Arjuna, Krishna's cousin, in the coming war of the Bharatas.
source_excerpt: 'O Govinda, he will be thy friend and help in battle... do thou instruct him in spiritual knowledge... always regard and take care of him as thou dost me.'

title: Krishna Sports with the Gopis in the Rasa Dance
one_line_summary: On autumnal moonlit nights, Krishna sports and dances with the gopis of Vraja, who are devoted to him.
source_excerpt: Thus encircled by the milk-women Krishna used to sport, of his own accord, in the autumnal night adorned by the moon.

title: Kansa Summons Krishna Through Akrura
one_line_summary: Fearing Krishna's growing power, Kansa orders Akrura to bring Krishna and Balarama to Mathura for the bow-sacrifice.
source_excerpt: 'Whatever it may be, O giver of gifts, go to Vraja, at my command and bring these two boys, Nanda and other Gopas who pay tributes to me.'
notes: Kansa also reveals, via Narada's report, that he knows Vasudeva exchanged the children; he publicly villifies Vasudeva, who bears it in silence.

title: Krishna Slays the Horse-Demon Keshi
one_line_summary: The horse-demon Keshi terrorizes Vrindavan; Krishna tears him apart, and Narada declares him Keshava.
source_excerpt: Krishna, stretching his hands a good deal, sundered him in twain... 'Since thou hast slain Keshi, thou shalt pass by the name of Keshava in the world.'

title: Akrura Arrives in Vraja and Beholds Krishna
one_line_summary: Akrura reaches Nanda's house and, seeing Krishna, adores him in his mind as Vishnu incarnate.
source_excerpt: As soon as he entered the gate... he saw Krishna stationed at the milking-place in the midst of calves like a bull... he praised him again and again.

title: Akrura Tells Krishna of His Parents' Suffering
one_line_summary: Akrura urges Krishna to come to Mathura, describing the misery of Vasudeva and Devaki under Kansa; Krishna agrees.
source_excerpt: 'O Krishna, that ascetic lady is being exhausted with your sorrow... do thou now make such an exertion... for saving thy aged parents overwhelmed with grief.'... Krishna... said 'So be it.'

title: Akrura Sees the Vision of Ananta in the Yamuna
one_line_summary: Bathing in the Yamuna, Akrura beholds the thousand-headed serpent Ananta with Vishnu on his lap, and is filled with wonder.
source_excerpt: sinking into the lake of Yamuna... he saw there the thousand-headed Deity Ananta... and the dark blue hued Vishnu... seated at ease on the lap of that king of serpents.

title: Krishna Slays the Insolent Washerman
one_line_summary: Entering Mathura, Krishna asks a washerman for clothes; when he answers insolently, Krishna strikes him dead.
source_excerpt: Krishna grew offended with him and struck him on the head with his fist strong as the thunder-bolt. With his head sundered he fell down lifeless on earth.
notes: The garland-maker Gunaka is separately blessed by Krishna with prosperity.

title: Krishna Straightens the Hunchback Kubja
one_line_summary: Krishna accepts unguents from the hunchback woman Kubja and, touching her, straightens her crooked form.
source_excerpt: Krishna, conversant with the art of arranging for sports, softly touched the haunch of Kuvja with his fingers... Knowing her haunch (thus) broken, the beautiful and sweet smiling Kuvja... said with love to Krishna.

title: Krishna Breaks Kansa's Great Bow
one_line_summary: Krishna takes up the great bow of Kansa, strings and bends it, and snaps it in two.
source_excerpt: Bent with force by Krishna that celebrated bow, resembling a serpent, broke in twain.

title: Kansa Orders the Wrestlers and the Elephant to Kill Krishna
one_line_summary: Kansa commands the wrestlers Chanura and Mushthika and the elephant Kuvalayapida to kill the two boys at the arena.
source_excerpt: 'Forsooth, fighting in the arena with those two forest-ranging cow-herd boys Krishna and Sangkarshana... you will be able to throw them on earth and kill them.'... 'Keep at the gate of the arena the... elephant Kuvalayapida.'

title: Krishna Kills the Elephant Kuvalayapida
one_line_summary: At the arena gate, the mad elephant Kuvalayapida attacks; Krishna tears out its tusks and slays it.
source_excerpt: placing his foot on his lower lip he, with his two hands, uprooted his tusks and struck him therewith... that huge elephant, with his tusks broken, fell down.

title: Krishna and Balarama Slay the Wrestlers
one_line_summary: In the arena, Krishna slays Chanura and Toshala, and Balarama slays Mushthika and Andhra.
source_excerpt: Wrestling with Chanura for a long time, Devaki's son... stole away his strength... struck him on the head with his fist... Thus with his eyes drawn out Chanura... lay in the arena.

title: Kansa Orders the Gopas Expelled and Vasudeva Punished
one_line_summary: Seeing his wrestlers slain, Kansa orders the cowherds expelled, Nanda bound, and Vasudeva punished; Krishna grows wrathful.
source_excerpt: 'Turn out of the arena these two sinful, grim-visaged and forest-ranging young cow-herds... punish him even today in such a way which persons not, aged, deserve.'

title: Krishna Drags Kansa from His Throne and Slays Him
one_line_summary: Krishna leaps upon Kansa's pavilion, drags him by the hair into the arena, and kills him.
source_excerpt: stretching his own Parigha-like arms Krishna drew Kansa by the hair in the arena... When... Kansa breathed his last Krishna threw away his body.

title: Balarama Slays Kansa's Brother; Krishna Greets His Parents
one_line_summary: Balarama kills Kansa's brother Urgita, and Krishna bows to his parents, who weep with joy.
source_excerpt: Holding powerfully by his hands the proud brother of Kansa, by name Urgita, the virtuous-souled Baladeva killed him... Having thus slain Kansa... the lotus-eyed Krishna first touched Vasudeva's feet.

title: Krishna Renounces the Kingdom and Installs Ugrasena
one_line_summary: Krishna refuses the throne, declares he has no need of the kingdom, and installs Ugrasena as king of Mathura.
source_excerpt: 'I do not care for the kingdom or the royal throne... place yourself on the throne and acquire victory by becoming the king.'... Govinda, well read in laws, installed him on the throne.

title: The Yadavas Perform Kansa's Funeral Rites
one_line_summary: With Krishna's consent, Ugrasena and the Yadavas perform Kansa's funeral rites on the bank of the Yamuna.
source_excerpt: desirous of performing the obsequial rites of king Kansa according to the ritualastic laws they placed his body in a palanquin and took it to the northern bank of Yamuna... setting fire to the pyre.

title: Krishna Retrieves Sandipani's Son from Yama's Abode
one_line_summary: As his teacher's fee, Krishna slays the demon Panchajana, takes the conch Panchajanya, and brings back Sandipani's dead son from Yama.
source_excerpt: The conch, which Janarddana obtained after slaying Panchajana, is known amongst gods and men as Panchajanya... having vanquished the fearful son of Vivaswan... obtained the child son of his preceptor.
notes: Story_arc 'other': the Sandipani episode (post-Kamsa youth and education) has no dedicated canonical arc.

title: Jarasandha Marches on Mathura to Avenge Kansa
one_line_summary: Learning of Kansa's death from his daughters Asti and Prapti, Jarasandha marches on Mathura with a host of allied kings.
source_excerpt: hearing of Kansa's death from his two daughters... the powerful Jarasandha, in no time, set out with his army... to slay all the Yadus.

title: Jarasandha Besieges Mathura
one_line_summary: Jarasandha's vast army surrounds Mathura and lays siege on all four gates.
source_excerpt: 'Let the armies of the kings united lay siege on all sides to this city.'

title: The Yadavas Battle Jarasandha's Army
one_line_summary: The Yadavas fight Jarasandha and his allies in a great battle, Rama and Jarasandha dueling with clubs.
source_excerpt: Thus did the great heroes and soldiers, belonging to the army of Vrishnis, fight for twenty-seven days with the highly powerful sovereigns and soldiers of the king of Magadha's party.

title: The Divine Voice Spares Jarasandha from Balarama
one_line_summary: As Balarama is about to strike Jarasandha with his mace, a heavenly voice declares Jarasandha is not to be slain by him; Jarasandha flees defeated.
source_excerpt: 'O Rama... this king of Magadha is not to be slain by thee... Jarasandha shall, in no time, meet with his death from the means that I have laid out for his destruction.'

title: The Yadavas Counsel That Mathura Cannot Withstand Siege
one_line_summary: The Yadavas tell Krishna that Mathura lacks walls and provisions and cannot withstand Jarasandha's repeated sieges.
source_excerpt: 'This city has a limited supply of food and fuels. It is not protected by a fort... It will not therefore be able to stand attack for even one day.'

title: Krishna Resolves to Abandon Mathura
one_line_summary: Krishna decides to leave Mathura with Balarama and head south, to draw Jarasandha away and protect the city.
source_excerpt: 'Therefore although I am capable, I shall, at this very moment, fly away with the worshipful Baladeva for saving my life like one incapable.'

title: Krishna Meets Parasurama, Who Counsels Gomanta
one_line_summary: On mount Sahya, Krishna meets the sage Parasurama, who counsels him to make his stand against Jarasandha on mount Gomanta.
source_excerpt: 'Getting upon that high summit... if you obstruct Jarasandha by fighting with him in the fort you will be able to conquer him.'

title: Garuda Restores Vishnu's Stolen Crown to Krishna
one_line_summary: Garuda, having recovered Vishnu's crown stolen by Bali's son, places it on Krishna's head on Gomanta.
source_excerpt: that foremost of birds threw from the welkin that crown on Vishnu's head... 'When I fell asleep in the ocean, Virochana's son... stole away my diadem... Garuda has brought this back.'
notes: The chapter also relates Balarama's intoxication by the Kadambari wine and the approach of the goddesses Varuni, Kanti and Sri.

title: Krishna Wields the Divine Weapons Against Jarasandha's Host
one_line_summary: On Gomanta, the divine weapons descend to Krishna and Balarama, who rout the kings; Balarama slays king Darada.
source_excerpt: came down for the two Yadavas four powerful Vaishnava weapons namely, the plough-share Samvartaka, the mace Sounanda, the discus Sudarshana, and the club Koumodaki.

title: The King of Chedi Befriends Krishna and Escorts Him to Karavira
one_line_summary: After Jarasandha flees, the king of Chedi, Krishna's kinsman by marriage, befriends him and escorts him to the city of Karavira.
source_excerpt: the highly effulgent king of Chedi, remembering his relationship with the Yadavas, approached Krishna... 'Let us go with our army and followers to the city of Karavira.'

title: Krishna Slays King Shrigala with the Discus
one_line_summary: King Shrigala of Karavira attacks Krishna, who slays him with the Sudarshana discus.
source_excerpt: holding up his discus he hurled it at Shrigala's breast... Shrigala too, having his heart pierced by the discus... fell down, bleeding like a cleft mountain.

title: Krishna Installs Shakradeva on the Throne of Karavira
one_line_summary: At the plea of Shrigala's queen, Krishna installs the slain king's son Shakradeva on the throne of Karavira.
source_excerpt: 'this son of Shrigala is just like mine. I declare safety unto them and gladly annoint him as the king.'... Placing the prince on the throne the powerful Janarddana sprinkled him with celestial water.
